lines.en: : Okay. What are you scheming today?
: Senpai! You say that as if I have a history of scheming. And I’ve been almost entirely scheme-free the whole time you’ve known me.
: Almost implies that there has been at least one. And that face is leading me to believe I am currently in the midst of it. So...out with it, subordinate.
: Hey! All that “subordinate” stuff really hurts, you know! I do just as much around here as you! You’d be nowhere without me.
: That’s probably true. Things would definitely be a lot quieter, though.
: Apology accepted.
There was no apology.
: To show your forgiveness, I will allow you to take me out to a fancy restaurant of your choice where I will proceed to-
: That is not what you came here for. Tell me what you want.
: Some respect would be nice.
: Anything else?
: Yeah. I have a secret for you.
: To be honest, things are about to get really crazy up in here, Sensei. You might wanna buckle up for this one.
: Uh-oh. Is today the day we finally cross the line of boss and semi-useful employee and wind up sleeping together on the couch?
: No! And for the millionth time, you are not my boss! I report only to those at the top of the educational ladder and I will not be reduced to mere nothingness by a man who can barely climb it!
: Sorry, can’t hear you from all the way above you on some ladder-thing.
: Newest employee of Kumon-mi High! Please enter the room!
: Newest employee?
: Ta-dah!
: Hey. I’m here now.
: What?
: Please give a warm welcome to the new light music club advisor, Rika Rokuhara!
: You’re...a teacher now?
: I hope not. I never even finished high school. I’m kind of just here to chaperone Rin’s band.
: And to refrain from nepotism by addressing them as the light music club and not “Rin’s band.”
: There was a job listing for just advising a club? You don’t have to, like...you know, teach as well?
: Yeah, I guess.
: What the fuck? I want that job.
: I mean...you kind of already have it, Senpai. You’re just not really good at that part either if what I’ve heard from the manga club is true.
: Stop talking to the girls in my club. Go hang out with your own.
: No can do, buddy. I need to hang on to every last bit of youth I’m able to wrap my hands around.
: Ignoring the slow disintegration of your psyche and how unhealthy your desire to be young again is, why are you making a show out of this? Rika could have just come in here without you.
: Because, jerk, you never answer your emails.
: I have emails?
: How do you still work here?
: Probably tenure. I’m not really sure.
: Hah...regardless, I’m here to save the day once again and let you know that it’s your responsibility to show Rika the ropes.
: I would have gladly done it, but the two of us have history.
: I’m surprised you have enough pride left to bring that “history” up.
: I must have been drunk. Either that or Rika just doesn’t have much experience when it comes to tonsil hockey.
: No comment.
: So I just have to show her the ropes?
: Yeah. Think you can handle it?
: Of course. Shouldn’t be a problem at all.
: Alright. Here they are.
: Cool. Thanks for showing me.
: So, now what?
: I’m not really sure. In fact, I barely even know what I’m supposed to be doing here.
: How did your orientation thingy go? Maybe you can just try and do that to me? Or...with me?
: On me?
: Orientation...
Come to think of it...I never had anything like that.
Sure, that’s most likely because I was thrust into this new (But confusingly not new) life in the middle of the school year where everyone already knew who I was and how I taught-
But that doesn’t take away from how confusing I know things must be for Rika right now. And how most other people in her shoes would just abuse their power to consensually molest a bunch of girls.
Actually, that’s probably just me and a handful of other horrible individuals who shouldn’t be allowed in a place like this. But I should ask just to make sure.
: How interested are you in pursuing a physical relationship with teenage girls?
: Like...in phys-ed? I can probably teach phys-ed if I have to. That wasn’t in the job description, but how hard could it possibly be?
Okay, so it seems like that sort of thing doesn’t even occur to Rika and I really am just the scum of the earth. That’s good.
But I should probably at least show her around so she doesn’t get lost and wind up like Yasu — desperately clinging to those she trusts and leaving her well-being entirely in their hands.
: I don’t think you’ll have to teach phys-ed. The girls normally just hang out on their phones for that period. But I can give you a tour at least.
: Cool. Works for me.
: I know we’re friends outside of work and whatnot, but I kind of need this job thing to go well so I can finally get out of Rin’s hair.
: I’m sure I don’t have to tell you this since you’re already familiar with the place, but let’s keep it professional while we’re here. Cool?
: Yeah...I don’t know if I can do that.
: Why? Do you have a crush on me?
: Why are your first assumptions for things always so strange?
: Is that strange? Because I don’t think I’ve ever had a job where my boss didn’t immediately try to hook up with me before, so I’m kind of just used to it by now.
: And how many times-
: No comment.
: I’m kidding.
: Well, kind of.
: The boss thing is true, but I haven’t really had many jobs in the first place so the numbers probably aren’t all that impressive or whatever.
: Why don’t we start with the gym?
For the next half-hour or so, I walk Rika around the school- pointing out the various rooms and offices she’ll probably have to familiarize herself with in the coming weeks.

But, to be honest, I have no idea if this will be valuable at all as I did not imagine the school would ever stoop to hiring someone for just one thing as the rest of us follow our classes everywhere.
Well, almost everywhere.
I’ve yet to make my way inside of the shower room in the gym yet, but I did come close that one time when Nodoka decided to try and ruin Yumi’s life.
Nodoka.
I keep forgetting what happened — but in different ways from how I normally forget.
That night in the hotel is all still a blur, but there’s something inside of me I cannot identify that doesn’t make me uncomfortable with it.
If anything, it makes me feel good.
The lingering satisfaction of unsheathing my cock from her virgin hole vaporizes the resentment and disdain I know I’m meant to have over what she’s done to Yumi and...anyone else she’s toyed with.
So basically...all of us.
But I can’t bring myself to hate her.
I can’t even bring myself to dislike her.
All I can think of is how safe she makes me feel.
Or perhaps it would be better described as numbness.
I want to feel it again.
I want to devour her.
: Helloooo? Anyone home?
: Huh? What?
: Caught you staring off into the distance. But I guess we can just chalk it up to you being a goober again.
: I don’t like whatever sort of “vibe” we’re creating here —which I’m pretty sure is what relationship dynamics are referred to as by young people now.
: Really? I think we mesh kinda well. But I’m saying that as professional Rika — not “make out with coworkers at a dive bar” Rika.
: As long as I’m next and not Wakana I’ll be happy.
: See?! I told you. Every single boss I’ve ever had has tried to get into my pants on day one. I can’t escape.
: I mean, if you want to get technical, I was trying to get into your mouth.
: That’s easier, but still. Come on, man. I’m too old to hang out under the bleachers at this point in life. I’m just trying to make some money so Rin doesn’t have to do my laundry anymore.
: Wait! Are we allowed to do our laundry here? Does the teacher’s lounge have a bed? Also, why is there a boy’s locker room? This is an all-girl school.
: No, no, and no clue. And before you ask, you can’t live here.
: Not even for, like...a weekend so Rin and Otoha can make out on her bed?
: Rika! What are you doing here? And what were you just saying about Rin and me?
: I work here now! I’m your new club advisor thing!
: Wait, seriously? Like, you officially work here? That’s awesome.
: It is! But do you know what’s even more awesome? The fact that you and Rin are sexually active n-
: Wow.
: Otoha! Come back! I just wanted to congratulate you guys!
: Rika, I get that you’re kind of...and forgive me for lack of a better term...a goober-
: But there are some things you just shouldn’t say to your daughter’s significant other and almost all of them are exactly what you just said.
: Damn it. I thought girls today were more open about that kind of stuff?

: Ignoring any thoughts or experience I have regarding that, I don’t think it really changes a girl not wanting to talk to her girlfriend’s mother about how many fingers she put inside of her daughter.
: I just wanted to express my appreciation. You have any idea how long Rin’s been hormonal for?

: Because that girl’s been spending way too long in the shower ever since she turned twelve and as someone who experienced that same burst of energy at that age, I know what's really going on in there.
: And that is...just one more thing a parent should just never reveal to anyone. So I am going to do my best to keep that little factoid away from Rin for the indefinite future.
: Oh, come on. She’s a kid. It’s not like I’m telling you about a grown woman’s habits. I bet you were the same exact way when you were that age.
: Maybe just...try to have a little more tact in the future.
: What future? I’m 42.
: And even if I look okay for my age, no one’s going to stick around when they find that out.
: People want families and whatnot and my time’s kind of limited, you know?
: Tact or no tact, it’s not gonna make a difference. So why not just “mom” it up while I still can?
: First off, you’re wrong and you have plenty of time left. Second, you can still “mom” it up and embarrass your daughter while keeping things like that a secret. And third-
: Is third something about how I’m a catch even with all of my “flaws?”
: Heh...
: You know, everybody always likes to say things like that.
: About how “perfection” isn’t real and that it’s those little “imperfections” that make us beautiful.
: And while that sounds nice and all...and makes us look like better people than we actually are, it’s all fake at the end of the day.
: Imperfections and flaws can be cute when they come in small doses, sure. But when you start paying close attention to little things like that, you don’t see “cute” at all.
: You see flaws as exactly what they are. Flaws. Flaws that pile up and weigh down how much you care about someone.
: If it’s one or two things, you can learn to deal with it.
: But then you start looking for more. And they start getting easier to find.
: Then, the next thing you know, you've collected so many of those “imperfections” that it becomes almost impossible to see anything good at all.
: No one has to be perfect, Rika.
: I agree. No one has to be perfect. No one can be perfect. Which is why we fall for people who ignore our flaws. And hey, for some, that kind of thing works out.
: There are plenty of successful couples who can live like that forever. And some who cherish those little quirks for the rest of their lives.
: But it’s impossible to know if you’re with someone like that beforehand.
: And by the time you figure it out, it might already be too late.
: I see...You’re not just worried you’re not good enough-
: I’m afraid of being wrong again.
: But, on the bright side, I’m not crying anymore. Now, it’s mostly just feeling like an idiot.
: I wasn’t always like this, though.
: Did you suffer some...traumatic brain injury or something?
: No, goober. I’ve never been book-smart or anything like that. Me and school were mortal enemies.
: But there were three things I was great at back before I spent all of my free time feeling sorry for myself.
: Thing number one was music.
: I might not be able to read it as well as a lot of famous composers and stuff, but that never really mattered to me.
: I made noise that made people feel good. Or sad. Or angry. Or whatever I wanted them to feel because I wanted to feel something too.
: I made money doing what I loved...and now I can make money doing that again. Just in a totally uncool, corporate kind of way. But hey, if Metallica can sell out, so can I.
: What’s number two?
: Protesting.
: Is that...a thing you can be good at?
: It got me thrown in jail a bunch of times. But like half of the shit teen Rika and company campaigned against wound up getting changed eventually, so hey. That’s a win in my book.
: It’s also how I met my ex.
: You two protested together?
: We were actually on opposite sides.
: She was always really straight-laced and traditional when it came to her values. But a lot of that was due to the environment she was brought up in.
: I was lucky enough to come from a more progressive household who let me form my own opinions instead of guiding me toward theirs.
: Which was really great on account of the whole “liking girls” thing.
: But yeah, if it weren’t for number two and number three, I never would have wound up with her in the first place.
: And what was number three exactly?
: Eating pussy.
: I expected nothing less from you.
: What can I say? Girls always like to think they’re straight until they meet someone who knows how to please them.
: So, yeah. I’m basically the savior of humanity — a woman so skilled that she has straight up eaten the homophobia out of someone.
: I’m curious as to how you got her in that position in the first place.
: I am just that good.
: But again, those days are over. I’m 100%% embarrassing mom now.
: Are you sure? Don’t you have a duty to the world you need to carry out? Not many were born with your power.
: The only duty I have now is getting my life back on track and making sure Rin stays on hers.
: Hopefully, I’ll be able to accomplish both of those by being here.
: And maybe...
: Maybe, I’ll find something else as well.
: Or maybe I won’t?
: There’s art in never knowing.
: And I don’t mind appreciating that for a little longer this time.
Rika’s affection has increased to [rika_love]!
